Animation sources

Our dashboard backgrounds use published cardiac imaging and licensed premade 3D animations. No source implies endorsement of Valus.

Cardiac MRI

Real-time MRI of a human heart (2-chamber view), Shuo Zhang, Martin Uecker, Dirk Voit, Klaus-Dietmar Merboldt, and Jens Frahm, 2010. Original publication. Licensed CC BY 2.0.

The original 463 × 463 footage is transcoded to WebM, looped, scaled, and feathered into the page background. We do not invent scan detail or interpolate anatomy. Original footage · Web version.

Firing neurons and immune cells

Animation of the anatomy and physiology of the human brain, Agnieszka Starostecka, 2023. Licensed CC BY 4.0. We excerpted 83.8–89.6 seconds for neurons and 90–94.5 seconds for immune cells, removed audio, and added a 0.6-second loop crossfade. Native 1920 × 1080 resolution, transcoded to VP9. These are illustrative 3D animations, not microscopy recordings. Neuron loop · Immune-cell loop.

DNA helix

Abstract 3D DNA Helix Animation in 4K, Tommaso Raso, via Pexels. Used under the Pexels License. This is an illustrative particle animation. Changes: excerpt from 1–11 seconds, silent VP9 conversion, downscaled from the downloaded 2560 × 1440 rendition to 1920 × 1080, and 0.6-second loop crossfade. The author does not endorse Valus.

Global Rankings brain scan

Side-view colored brain reference supplied by the site owner. Original creator and imaging modality have not been independently verified. Displayed with a subtle zoom and theme-aware edge blending; this is presentation motion applied to a still image, not recorded PET activity.

Overview

Student and instructor Overview pages use the original Valus procedural bloodstream animation, rendered in real time and centered in the workspace. It responds to light/dark themes and reduced-motion preferences.

Previously used blood-cell footage

This asset is retained in the source tree but is no longer used on Overview.

RedWhiteBloodCells, Dimit09. Licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. The adapted blood-cell loop is also distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0, attribution Dimit09 / Valus adaptation. Changes: GIF-to-VP9 conversion, repeated frames at 30 fps and 0.6-second loop crossfade. Original 600 × 400 resolution retained; no additional source detail is claimed.

All background excerpts are centered, scaled to the viewport, and blended with a theme-aware veil. Original authors do not endorse Valus. Reduced-motion settings pause playback.

Earlier neuron reconstruction

The following reconstruction remains in the source tree but is no longer used as the dashboard background.

cnic_001 / NMO_1, Wearne/Hof archive, retrieved through NeuroMorpho.Org (RRID:SCR_002145). CC BY 4.0 reuse terms. Source 3D reconstruction.

This is a rhesus macaque prefrontal layer-3 pyramidal neuron reconstruction containing soma and dendrites, not an axon or a human brain network. The visualization repeats and transforms the measured skeleton, thickens fine structures for visibility, and adds illustrative spines, organelles, surface shading, and traveling fluorescent signals. The colors and activity are not recorded electrophysiology.

  • Original reconstruction publications: doi:10.1016/S0306-4522(02)00305-6 and doi:10.1093/cercor/13.9.950.
  • Tecuatl C, Ljungquist B, Ascoli GA (2024). Accelerating the continuous community sharing of digital neuromorphology data. FASEB Bioadv. 6(7):207–221. doi:10.1096/fba.2024-00048.
  • Adapted geometry and visualization additions based on this reconstruction are available under CC BY 4.0, attribution: Valus and the reconstruction sources above.

Visual research

Dendritic Spines in a Hippocampal Neuron, Miquel Bosch, Bear Lab, Picower Institute, MIT, provided a microscopy reference for spine shapes. The reference photograph is not redistributed in this website.

We also evaluated Versal’s neuron mesh, Ehab Shalout’s animated heart cross-section, and Allen Cell Types. These assets are not included.
